claims.text: The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have a random distribution of atomic species.
Compositional fluctuations in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles produce localized lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions reduce local atomic cohesive forces.
Reduced local cohesive forces lower the effective melting temperature of the affected regions.
Regions having locally reduced cohesive energy act as nucleation sites for premelting.
Premelting begins preferentially in locally unstable, compositionally distorted regions.
Melting progresses heterogeneously from the nanoparticle surface toward the core.
Relative to homogeneous metal nanoparticles, FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will begin surface disorder at a lower temperature.
FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will form amorphous, liquid-like regions below the bulk melting point.
The spatial progression of the melting front will correlate with regions of greatest lattice distortion.
Before heating, the nanoparticles are fully crystalline and show no premelting features.
The proposed mechanism applies within a nanoparticle size range in which surface effects are significant.
Changing particle size may alter or obscure the proposed premelting mechanism.
A reactive atmosphere may alter or obscure the proposed premelting mechanism.
Failure to observe earlier or spatially heterogeneous premelting, or failure to find a correlation between local composition or distortion and melting onset, would falsify the hypothesis.
